This quiz will cover everything we've covered in foundations of R assignments.

1. Open the tidyverse library.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

2. Open the starwars dataset.
```{r}
data(starwars)
```

3. Create a subset of data that contains only the humans from the starwars franchise.
```{r}
humanStarWars <-subset(starwars, starwars$species == "Human")
humanStarWars
```

4. In this subset of data, who is the tallest character? 

**Darth Vader, since he is 202 cm. I dont know if you want me to find it with code though? I'm checking my notes and I can't find anything that would be useful!**
```{r}
print(humanStarWars |> select(name, height))
# Darth Vader since he has 202. 

#if you wanted something more interesting, hopefully this satisfies you?
subset(humanStarWars, humanStarWars$height >= 200)
```

5. In this subset of data, print the information about the character in the third row.
```{r}
print(humanStarWars[3,])
```

6. In the full starwars dataset, calculate the average mass for the masculine characters. 
```{r}
mean(starwars$mass[starwars$gender =="masculine"], na.rm=TRUE)
#106.5149
```

7. Create a dataset that contains only the characters and the films that they appeared in from the full dataset. 
```{r}
CharacterFilm <- starwars |> select(name, films)
```

8. Create a new column in the starwars dataset that contains a "ranking" of all characters (Note: you don't have to ac
tually rank them. Just fill the column in with the numbers 1-87)
```{r}
starwars$rank <- 1:87
starwars |> select(name, rank)
```

9. Create a subset of data for the characters from Naboo. How many characters are from Naboo? 
```{r}
nabooSubset <- subset(starwars, starwars$homeworld == "Naboo")
nrow(nabooSubset)
# 11
```

10. How many droids are in the full dataset? 
```{r}
nrow(subset(starwars, starwars$species == "Droid"))
# 6
```
